# Elis

> A terminal workspace for AI coding agents on macOS and Linux, with a full control API

Elis is a native terminal for macOS and Linux (engines: libghostty on macOS, Konsole on Linux), with a deliberately small interface and a full control API. Instead of scattering sessions across tabs, it groups them into named workspaces, and almost everything that structure holds is also an object a script can address: the bundled elisctl creates and types into sessions, runs overlays, moves windows, sets a session's status glyph, and reads that state back over a local socket. Running many AI coding agents at once is the obvious use, and far from the only one. With nothing scripted it is a fast, modern general-purpose terminal for everyday work.

## Key Features

- Vertical sidebar: workspaces grouping their sessions, with drag-reorder, a flagged working-set view, and single-workspace focus; companion sessions (a shell, a program or an HTML page) pin under a session and move, fold and close with it, on remote sessions too; an HTML page can also be a session of its own that holds companions
- Agent-status glyphs on sidebar rows: active, blocked, completed, idle — auto-wired for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode
- elisctl control CLI over a local unix-domain socket: create, rename, move, and type into sessions, run overlays, move windows, capture output, post notifications tied to a session
- Installable agent skill that teaches Claude Code and Codex the control model and the full elisctl command set
- Surfaces per session: split panes (two shells), a per-session scratch terminal, and floating/full overlays that run a program or show a local HTML page or a URL, where a local page can run Elis commands and hand a choice back to its caller; plus one app-wide quick terminal in a floating panel, summonable by a system-wide hotkey
- Remote sessions: attach a live session from another Mac running Elis over ssh, together with its companions, with its status, context, notifications, HUD and the layout of attached panes mirrored to the attaching Mac, and its questions and program overlays drawn there
- Remote server: elis-server runs sessions on a Linux host as zmx daemons under a systemd user service, and a Mac remote window mirrors its workspaces and sessions over pooled ssh, keeping them running across disconnects; installed from the Mac with elisctl server install HOST, which downloads the matching aarch64 or x86_64 release and checks it against the sha256 the app was built with
- Multi-window: a library of windows (e.g. "work" and "personal"), one per screen, restored on next launch
- 512 bundled themes with a live-preview picker, fully rebindable kitty-flavored keymap.conf, event hooks in hooks.conf that run a shell line on status, session, pane and tree events, and full session persistence
- In-terminal search, fuzzy command palettes, and a Ctrl-Tab MRU session switcher

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://naiksoftware.github.io/elis/docs): full reference — install, keybindings, keymap.conf, hooks.conf, ghostty config, themes, control API
- [Control API commands](https://naiksoftware.github.io/elis/commands): the complete elisctl command catalog
- [README](https://github.com/NaikSoftware/elis/blob/master/README.md): the project synopsis, with install, the model, and the control-API demo
- [Architecture](https://github.com/NaikSoftware/elis/blob/master/macos/ARCHITECTURE.md): module split, surface ownership, and the libghostty C boundary

## Install

- [Releases](https://github.com/NaikSoftware/elis/releases/latest): the macOS DMG (Apple Silicon, macOS 14+, not notarized) and the Android APK
- [Linux](https://github.com/NaikSoftware/elis/tree/master/linux): the Qt6/KDE app, built from source

## Optional

- [Home page](https://naiksoftware.github.io/elis): feature overview and screenshots
- [Source](https://github.com/NaikSoftware/elis): MIT licensed; embeds libghostty from Ghostty (MIT) on macOS and Konsole on Linux
